# driftd

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/JStrueder/driftd/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/JStrueder/driftd/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![test-coverage](https://github.com/JStrueder/driftd/actions/workflows/test-coverage.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/JStrueder/driftd/actions/workflows/test-coverage.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

driftd is a wrapper around the [rtdists](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=rtdists) package (Singmann, Brown, Gretton, & Heathcote) that makes it easier to fit the diffusion decision model to response time data and to analyze the results. You specify which parameters vary across which conditions; driftd builds the likelihood, fits it to each participant by maximum likelihood, and provides standard errors, analysis-ready parameter tables, model fit checks, model comparison, parameter and model recovery, and simulation. All diffusion model computations are done by rtdists.

## Installation

Install the current release from GitHub with [pak](https://pak.r-lib.org):

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("JStrueder/driftd@v0.1.0")
```

To get the latest development version instead, use `pak::pak("JStrueder/driftd")`.

The vignette is a complete worked analysis, from the data to reporting. To install it along with the package:

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("JStrueder/driftd@v0.1.0", build_vignettes = TRUE)
vignette("driftd", package = "driftd")
```

## Quick example

The example data, `speed_acc`, are from a lexical decision experiment with speed and accuracy instructions (Wagenmakers et al., 2008), as distributed with rtdists. Fitting all 17 participants takes about 15 minutes per model, so the code is not run here; the vignette shows the output.

```{r example, eval = FALSE}
library(driftd)
data(speed_acc)

# boundary separation by instruction, drift rate by stimulus type
fit <- driftd(speed_acc, sub_id = "id", response = "response", rt = "rt",
              vary_a = "condition", vary_v = "stimulus", fix_st0 = FALSE)
fit$summary
estimates(fit)                     # one row per participant and parameter, with SEs
estimates(fit, format = "cells")   # one row per participant and condition

# model fit
pred <- predict(fit, seed = 1)
plot(pred)                         # RT quantiles
plot(pred, type = "choice")        # response probabilities
summary(pred)                      # participants with the most misfit

# model comparison: does the instruction also affect the drift rate?
fit_v <- driftd(speed_acc, sub_id = "id", response = "response", rt = "rt",
                vary_a = "condition", vary_v = c("stimulus", "condition"), fix_st0 = FALSE)
cmp <- compare_models(a = fit, a_v = fit_v)
plot(cmp)

# parameter and model recovery
plot(recover_parameters(fit, seed = 1))
plot(recover_models(a = fit, a_v = fit_v, seed = 1))

# simulate data from the fitted model
sims <- simulate(fit, nsim = 10, seed = 1)
```

## Interactive parameter explorer

The [DDM Parameter Explorer](https://jstrueder.github.io/driftd/explorer/) shows in the browser how drift rate, boundary separation, starting point and non-decision time change simulated choices and response times. To use it offline, download [`docs/explorer/index.html`](docs/explorer/index.html) and open it in any browser.

## Outliers

By default, every trial must be explained by the diffusion model, so a few fast guesses or lapses can distort the estimates; remove anticipations (e.g. RTs below 0.15 s) before fitting. For robustness against contaminant trials that trimming misses, `p_outlier` adds an outlier component as in HDDM (Wiecki, Sofer, & Frank, 2013): each trial's likelihood becomes a mixture of the diffusion model density and a uniform outlier density. It is fixed, not estimated, and off by default (`p_outlier = 0`). See `?driftd` for details.

```r
fit_robust <- driftd(speed_acc, sub_id = "id", response = "response", rt = "rt",
                     vary_a = "condition", vary_v = "stimulus", fix_st0 = FALSE,
                     p_outlier = 0.02)
```

## Credits

driftd is built on [rtdists](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=rtdists) (Singmann, Brown, Gretton, & Heathcote), which computes all diffusion model densities, distribution functions and random numbers, based on the fast-dm code of Andreas and Jochen Voss. If you use driftd, please cite rtdists as well; `citation("driftd")` gives both references.

The `speed_acc` example data were collected by Wagenmakers, Ratcliff, Gomez, and McKoon (2008, Experiment 1) and are taken from the rtdists package.

Wagenmakers, E.-J., Ratcliff, R., Gomez, P., & McKoon, G. (2008). A diffusion model account of criterion shifts in the lexical decision task. *Journal of Memory and Language, 58*(1), 140-159. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jml.2007.04.006
